correctness.rationale: For the implication operation on nonempty subsets, the term-definable union and Boolean principal intervals force existing-meet preservation. Each output coordinate induces a nonempty subset of singleton inputs; nonempty-meet preservation forces this subset to be a singleton or the entire set. This yields the exhaustive pointed-function normal form. Every allowable pointed function satisfies implication coordinatewise. The image is an r-cube above the nonempty sentinel fiber, or the full punctured cube for a permutation. Surjection counting yields binomial(n,r)*(r+1)!*Stirling(n,r+1) and total (n+1)^n-n^n+n!. The reversed composition law equates idempotence with theta^2=theta; selecting r nonzero fixed roots and requiring a sentinel preimage yields binomial(n,r)*((r+1)^(n-r)-r^(n-r)). Explicit algebraic quantifiers apply for all integers n>=2. Independent brute-force implication-preservation tests for n=2,3,4 agree, but these finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural finite algebra representing implication-only classical logic, the rank spectrum of its endomorphism monoid and which images occur as retractions are structural invariants determining the kinds and numbers of quotient/retract representations. The theorem yields a complete classification for every carrier size rather than a small-case census, sharply distinguishes Boolean image lattices from the punctured whole image, and supplies exact rank-refined idempotent counts. These are motivated concrete algebraic invariants with reuse for studying the endomorphism monoid; no further application is assumed.
